II. FRIEDRICH NIETZSCHE: The Persian Prophet's Invasion

Historical Record

  • Date: Summer 1881, specifically July-August
  • Location: Sils-Maria, Swiss Alps (elevation 6,000 ft)
  • Context: Nietzsche had resigned from Basel University due to health collapse; was in deep physical and mental crisis

Primary Source Evidence

  • Letter to Franz Overbeck, August 14, 1881: "Zarathustra stole upon me, I was not free to choose whether he came... Has anyone at the end of the 19th century a clear idea of what poets of strong eras called inspiration?"
  • Ecce Homo (written 1888, published 1908): "Zarathustra himself, as a type... he stole upon me... one would have to feel that one is no more than a mere incarnation, a mere mouthpiece, a mere medium of overpowering forces."
  • Thus Spoke Zarathustra (published 1883-1885): The entire work is the product of this experience

Secondary Verification

  • Philosophy Now magazine (Issue 139, 2023) documents: "Nietzsche experienced a vision during his Alpine walks where he felt Zarathustra as an external, communicating presence."
  • Walter Kaufmann's Nietzsche: Philosopher, Psychologist, Antichrist (1950) dedicates Chapter 4 to this phenomenon, calling it "the most documented mystical experience in modern philosophy."
